correctness.rationale: Read inverse letters right-to-left in a forward word. Inverse a rotates occupancy and crossing indices by -1; inverse b copies the bit at d into 0. A shrinking copy clears 0 when d is empty; its incoming edge loses any crossing, and the outgoing edge still cannot be a 0-to-1 crossing. Non-growing copies thus cannot create crossings. In every path to a larger set the first growth is a copy, with some original surviving crossing rotated to 0; fewer than r=min E_d rotations cannot do that. The word ba^r attains r+1. No crossings means constant occupancy on each d-orbit; rotations preserve this condition and copies then fix the set, so the infinity case covers precisely the unions of the orbits. With gcd=1, ignoring starting edges i>=t leaves disjoint directed paths for t<n, each allowing exactly the nonincreasing binary strings, v+1 per path. At t=n only the two constants remain, and differences cancel those constants at all lengths. The final deleted edge has source n-1 and the path starts at n-1+d, proving the unique longest set of each size; d=1 gives the single explicit path and isolated vertices. Independent preimage-layer BFS, using preimages built from forward maps, agreed on 45 automata and 16,298 nontrivial subsets, both n=7 example vectors, all coprime path products, and the claimed extremizers. Finite enumeration is supplemental.
residual_risks: The full histogram is for coprime displacements. The proof does not cover general rank-defect-one maps or imply reset or image-avoidance thresholds.
